title: 进来, 出去, 回来: direction after a verb
summary: Lets you show which way a movement goes, as in 他走进来了.
structure: Verb + 进 / 出 / 回 / 上 / 下 + 来 / 去
Verb + 进 / 回 + Place + 来 / 去
explanation:
来 after a verb means movement TOWARDS the speaker, 去 means AWAY: 进来 'come in', 进去 'go in', 出来 'come out', 回去 'go back'. They can follow other verbs too: 走进来 'walk in', 跑出去 'run out', 拿回来 'bring back'.

A place goes before 来 / 去: 他回家去了 'He went back home', 你进教室来吧 'Come into the classroom.' Ask yourself: where is the speaker? That decides 来 or 去.

mistakes.why: The place goes before 来 / 去.
Towards the speaker is 来: I'm outside, so you come OUT to me (出来).

why: Correct: down towards the speaker = 下来.
下去 is down and away from the speaker.

exercises.en: He's in the room. You go in.
why: Correct: the speaker is outside, so going in is 进去.
进来 would mean coming in towards the speaker.
家 must come before 来.

exercises.en: She walked out of the classroom.

exercises.instruction: You're at home; ask your friend to come over.
why: Don't mix 去 and 来.
来 and 去 can't go together like this.

exercises.prompt: The teacher is in the classroom and says to a student at the door:
why: Correct: come in towards the teacher = 进来.
进去 would mean the teacher is outside.
